properties.description: Details the classification-as-RL formulation, framing NIDS as an environment.
Deep dive into CICIDS2017 flaws, preprocessing requirements, and evaluation.
Dataset comparison table, focusing on historical evolution from KDDCup99 to modern sets.
Theoretical and implementation background for applying QRDQN to NIDS.
Dossier on reward and cost-sensitive design for NIDS, highlighting FP/FN asymmetries.
Master research map grouping literature by taxonomy (datasets, ML, RL, methodology, etc.).
Executive source map covering flow-based NIDS, DRL for IDS, and methodological warnings.
Deep dive into DRL-IDS literature, noting dominance of DQN, lack of distributional RL, and poor evaluation practices.
Dataset comparison matrix and deep dive into CICIDS2017 limitations and leakage risks.
Action space for the agent classifying flows into benign (PERMIT) or malicious (BLOCK).
Reward function design where False Negatives (FN) incur a higher penalty than False Positives (FP) due to higher risk.
RL formulation where each dataset record acts as an environment state and classification acts as an action.
Common pitfalls like random row-wise splits, temporal leakage, class imbalance, and lack of external validation.
Splitting datasets chronologically or by scenario to prevent leakage, as opposed to random row-wise splits.
Using independent lab-captured traffic to validate models and address poor cross-dataset generalization.
Primary dataset for offline training/validation, features realistic traffic but suffers from temporal leakage under random splits.
Distributional Deep RL model used as the core defender agent, learning risk-sensitive policies.
